title: The Dog Night, 2012
logline: Thirteen years. Drawn in the new line: the dumpster has never been so exact. The dog has never been so old.

panels.composition: The dumpster, night, the bulb — drawn in Era III's line: every rivet, every rust bloom, the chain-link's exact weave. WOOD setting BARNABY down.

image.prompt: a man setting an old dog down behind a bowling alley at night before a rusted dumpster rendered with precise architectural ink line, every rivet and rust bloom exact, a bare bulb, no words

panels.composition: The dog. Thirteen. Cataracts. Drawn without pity and without looking away.

image.prompt: close-up of a very old dog's face with clouded eyes under a bulb, drawn plainly and tenderly in clean ink, no words

panels.composition: Wood sitting. The dog in his lap, entirely. He's small enough now.

characters.pose: sitting, the dog in his lap

image.prompt: a man sitting on gravel at night with an old dog curled entirely in his lap, bulb light, no words

panels.composition: The sign. SMALL WOOD LANES, the S dark, and now the second L dark too. Wood carrying the dog under it.

image.prompt: a man carrying an old dog beneath a bowling-alley neon sign where two letters have gone dark, night, clean ink with one spot tone, no words
image.notes: Two letters dark: S and the second L. Track it.

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays
